newsitem.title: USA: Capital gains tax should be under 20 pct--Lott.
newsitem.headline: Capital gains tax should be under 20 pct--Lott.

text.p: U.S. Senate Majority Leader Trent Lott said Monday he would like to see the capital gains tax under 20 percent.

Lott, who was speaking at a luncheon hosted by the Economic Club of Chicago here, said that the capital gains tax cut was not specified in Friday's balanced budget agreement and that the decision would be up to the Senate Finance Committee and the House Ways and Means Committee.
"I think we ought to let them look at it and what will be best for the economy," Lott told reporters.
Lott said the committees have the option of making a capital gains tax cut retroactive. He said the only limitation on a capital gains tax cut would be within the gross tax cut numbers.
"You would have to allow room for tax credits and other components, but I think there is enough there to get it down into that range of under 20 percent," Lott said.
